title: The normalized algebraic-connectivity Nordhaus-Gaddum conjecture
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, let $G^c$ be its complement, and let $\lambda_2(G)$ denote the second-smallest eigenvalue of the normalized Laplacian of $G$.

**Normalized algebraic-connectivity conjecture.**

$$
\lambda_2(G)+\lambda_2(G^c)\leq 2-O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\right).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by focus graphs, for which the two normalized algebraic connectivities approach $1$ while their sum approaches $2$. The supplied text does not provide a proof, disproof, or further resolution.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12751

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2026). “The Laplacian spread is defined as $s(G) = \mu_n(G) - \mu_2(G)$. The Laplacian spread conjecture was posited in 2011 by Zhai et al. and then proved in 2021 by Einollahzadeh and Karkhaneei .”
source_name: Mark Kempton, Xavier Zaitzeff and Sibi Muthuprakash, “Nordhaus-Gaddum upper bounds for graph connectivity parameters”, arXiv:2606.12751 (2026).
